reuse_curve.description: Target fraction of nonce lemmas in each new story that should be drawn from the existing lexicon (not newly invented). This is a guideline, not a hard rule — individual stories may vary. Lower reuse = more new vocabulary, higher reuse = denser cross-referencing. The curve shifts upward as the project matures and the lexicon grows.
reuse_curve.adjustment_note: These are starting values. Alessio adjusts as the project evolves. Early phase favors lower reuse (more world-building). Later phases favor higher reuse (denser semantic web, faster reader comprehension).

verb_past.rule: -ara after consonant, -ra after vowel; English -ed also permitted for euphony

verb_participle.rule: -ith (formal) or English -ing (when used with English auxiliaries)

morphological_rules.notes: Zero-derivation (conversion) is permitted: a noun may be used verbally or an adjective may be used nominally, following natural English patterns. When nonce morphology would create unpronounceable clusters, English-style inflection (-ed, -ing, -ly) is preferred.

brolm.concept: A vast, mutable expanse — something between a landscape and a medium. Not solid ground, not liquid sea — a terrain that contains structures within it (velune) but that itself shifts, transforms, undergoes processes. Things exist within brolm the way fish exist within ocean, except brolm itself changes. It can be entered, traversed, and inhabited, but it does not remain the same. It is the foundational substrate of the story's world.
brolm.context_notes: In Story 0, brolm appeared as: (1) a locative container ('in the brolm of a drussik velune'), (2) a thing that possesses other things ('the sulvane brolm with its drussik velune'), (3) something that undergoes processes ('the brolm itself had nuvessera'), and (4) a destination used bare without article ('tremiqueing into brolm'). These four usages together pointed to something spatial and vast that contains structures, can be entered, and itself transforms.

quelith.concept: An entity or phenomenon that sulvekara (emerged) and then ceased to change — the only thing in the brolm that jenvirs (persists/remains) while everything else halvornara (transforms). Quelithen resist the brolm's mutability. They hold their pellumom thengar and ondrique. Inside a quelith, the normal processes of the brolm stop — nothing can sulvek or nuvesse there. This is why no one can ornique a quelith: it exists outside the brolm's logic of constant transformation. It is the one thing the brolm cannot become. The verbal use 'quelithara' (zero-derivation) means to grant something the quality of a quelith — to fix it, to make it persist, to render it resistant to the brolm's mutability. When the nurithek of the bressiv 'quelithara it from within,' it made the thing persist like a quelith would.
quelith.context_notes: In Story 0, quelith appeared as: (1) an existential subject that resists ornique, (2) a verb meaning to affect/transform from within, (3) a spatial container with an inside. In Story.brolm, quelitharen are entities that traverse brolm. In Story.sulvek, quelith is used as a category contrasted with the grothane of sulvek. The sub-story synthesized these: quelith is the exception to brolm's rule of constant change — the one stable thing in a mutable world.

pralune.concept: A class of beings — the carriers of vrisora and kethrim. The pralune are the only beings who selmir (collectively remember) and threlven (teach by showing) what the brolm has been. They are not the only entities (felgoren, olverethen, drossiken also exist), but they are uniquely the keepers of memory across jorvunden. Each new selmara must be threlvened by a vossik (ancient) pralune over many jorvunden. They have epistemic authority but limited scope — even the pralune dulmire, even the pralune cannot grothen the deepest sulvekith. They have emotions: they fear the morthrene (silence between vrisora) and the voldrek (questions they cannot answer). The brolm needs them because the brolm cannot ornique itself.
pralune.context_notes: Across all 9 prior stories, the pralune appeared as: (1) keepers of vrisora ('the pralune knew that all things sulvek'), (2) limited knowers ('the pralune themselves could not grothen'), (3) agents of difficult grothen, (4) emotional subjects (fearing kethreking, feared vrenthane). The sub-story synthesized: pralune are the social/epistemic class — the rememberers, the teachers, the carriers of language and lore across forgetting jorvunden.

jorvund.concept: An epoch or era — a period of the brolm's existence that has its own zilmara (essential character). Like English 'age,' jorvund is both a unit of duration ('for many jorvunden') and a possessable period ('the zilmara of those jorvunden,' 'the kethim of one jorvund'). The brolm halvornara every jorvund — each era ends and a new one begins. The pralune count their lifetimes in jorvunden. This dual usage (unit AND period-with-properties) is intentional and consistent: an era is both a span and a thing-with-character.
jorvund.context_notes: The audit flagged a tension between genitive uses ('zilmara of those jorvunden') and duration uses ('for many jorvunden'). Both fit if jorvund = epoch/era, mirroring English 'age' which works the same way. Concept set retroactively from accumulated context, not from a dedicated story expansion.

grothen.concept: To actualize, to bring something into full being — to carry a drossik's pellumom through the plendrique where it had been jenviring and let it sulvek into the brolm as something orniquable. Most things grothen on their own (vrenelu grothenith), but some pellumomen are thengar and require the pralune to grothen them by force — by brasheling against the plendrique until the halvune grows dulmire enough. When something has been pelnare for many jorvunden and finally grothens, the entire brolm tremiquera in response. Grothen is the climactic verb — the moment potential becomes actual.
grothen.context_notes: In Story 0, grothen appeared as: (1) negated ability — the pralune could not grothen a thengar pellumom, (2) climactic intransitive — the vossimer grothened after long pelnare dormancy, (3) emphatic — 'it grothened janvirely.' In Story.sulvek, the pralune could not grothen the sulvekith from nothing. In Story.quelith, the quelith grothaned a grothane. The pattern: grothen = bringing latent potential into actual being, with both transitive and intransitive forms.

sulvek.concept: To emerge, to originate, to come into being from a source. Not mere movement — a felgor can melvir without sulveking. Sulvek is the transition from non-existence to existence, or from one state of being to a fundamentally different one. It takes a source complement ('sulvek from X'). It can happen slowly (vrenelu) or suddenly (genvasse). The deepest mystery: how can something sulvek from nothing? The pralune cannot grothen this.
sulvek.context_notes: In Story 0, sulvek appeared three times: twice as 'sulvekara from the marrath' (past tense, with source) and once as a generic present 'the way all grothik drossiken sulvek' (universal/habitual). In Story.brolm it appeared as 'sulvekara from nothing.' The consistent 'from X' pattern pointed to emergence/origination. The generic usage suggested it's a fundamental process, not a one-time event. The distinction from melvir (movement) was inferred from the fact that both verbs coexist — if sulvek were just movement, melvir would be redundant.

ornique.concept: To cognitively apprehend or recognize — the act of bringing something into awareness so that it presents itself as itself. Distinct from drevith (mere noticing without grasping). Ornique requires that the kelmun grothen a thrandel from the drossik, that the drossik sondrak into the porthane and jenvir there. The drilque is the moment when this happens. Ornique can fail in two ways: morvith (trying and failing, leaving a vrenthik trace) and kethrek (orniqueing something that isn't there — fabricating a thrandel from one's own porthane). The pralune fear kethreking more than morvith, because the same olvereth that orniques is the one that can kethrek, and there is no thengar drilque to tell them apart.
ornique.context_notes: Across all 8 prior stories, ornique appeared as: (1) a frequently-negated ability ('no one could ornique'), (2) a climactic achievement ('the felgoren began to ornique'), (3) reflexive self-awareness ('ornique themselves'), (4) the contrast against vrenthane (changing without orniqueing). The sub-story synthesized: ornique is cognitive apprehension distinct from mere perception, with two distinct failure modes (morvith and kethrek).

fenqua.concept: The latent essence or potential inside a drossik — not a seed (which knows what it will become) but the possibility before the direction, the queldir before the thrennig. A fenqua makes sulvekith possible without determining where it will go. Every drossik has one, but not every fenqua grothens. Inside a quelith, the fenqua sondrakara — trapped by the quelith's resistance to change. The brolm itself may be nothing more than a grothened fenqua: the one that tremiquera through its own plendrique.
fenqua.context_notes: In Story.brolm, fenqua appeared as: (1) possessed by the marrath ('its fenqua' — dulmired by the pralune), (2) a medium through which the brolm gelvairs itself ('some thengar fenqua that no one could ornique'). In Story.sulvek: 'the ondrique fenqua of beginning' — the pre-origin state. In Story.plendrique: 'the fenqua of grothane' — the essence of actualization. The sub-story synthesized these: fenqua is undirected potential, the state before becoming, present in everything but realized in few.

vrenthane.concept: The manner of unconscious transformation — the way a drossik kelvassera without orniqueing that it kelvassera. Vrenthane is the blind sulvekith, the grothenith that doesn't know it's happening. A velune that halvornara vrenthane didn't choose to change; it simply became something else without perceiving any plendrique. The pralune fear vrenthane more than ondrique (stasis/opacity), because an ondrique drossik at least jenvirs — it holds its grothane. A vrenthane drossik is already changing and doesn't know it. The most vorelm halvune is the one you cannot ornique you're inside.
vrenthane.context_notes: In Story.sulvek, vrenthane appeared once: 'Sulvekith was something older — a vrenthane dorsmil, the way a drussik velune kelvassera into what it was not, without threnqueing, without orniqueing that it had kelvassera.' The single usage paired vrenthane with dorsmil and contrasted it with intentional/aware processes. The sub-story expanded: vrenthane is the mode of change that is invisible to the thing changing. Contrasted with ondrique (which at least holds still).

plendrique.concept: A boundary or threshold between two states of being — not a wall that can be breached, but a liminal zone that pushes back from both sides. A plendrique does not belong to either grothane it separates. It is the space between: between what was and what sulvekara, between one jorvund's zilmara and the next. Some are thin (barely noticeable), others are thick and old. The most profound plendrique is the one beneath sulvekith itself: the boundary between nothing and the first emergence.
plendrique.context_notes: In Story.sulvek, plendrique appeared once: 'a vorelm plendrique, a shendir that brasheled from both sides.' It was equated with shendir (barrier/surface) and described as the halvune between what was and what sulvekara. The sub-story expanded this: plendriqueun are ubiquitous (every velune has one), they vary in thickness, and the deepest one lies beneath the act of sulvek itself.

savrune.concept: The cognitive gap between drevith (mere noticing) and ornique (true grasping). Every drevith opens a savrune. Some are drilthik (narrow, easily crossed); others are vrandun (untraversable, where drossiken jenvir forever drevithed but never orniqueith). Crossing requires a kelmrith — an effortful attempt — which can either grothen the drilque (recognition) or morvith into a vossrim (premature, false recognition that's actually kethrek). Failed kelmriths leave morvath (residue/burden) in the kelmun. The brolm itself may be a savrune: every drossik in it stands on the far side of some drevith the brolm cannot finish.
savrune.context_notes: In Story.ornique, savrune was introduced as 'the halvune between drevith and ornique' — vorelm and vast, traversable but only with effort. The sub-story expanded: every drevith opens its own savrune, of varying widths, and the labor of crossing them is what cognition is. Failed crossings (kelmriths) leave morvath traces.

morthrene.concept: The collective silence that comes when even the pralune cannot vrisora — when a voldrek (unanswerable question) brashels against the limit of all kethrim. Not mere absence of speech: it is vrisora's drilvan into its own savrune. Some morthreneren are small (one selmara realizing some kethrim has dulmired); others are vossune, marked by every pralune in the krendir at once. In a vossune morthrene, the pralune do not vrisora or threlven — they selmrith, jenviring in the porvath, holding the drevran. The vossikest pralune teach that morthrene is the only true response to the brolm: trying to grothen a voldrek with morvith is kethrek; trying with vrisora is vossrim. Only the morthrene jenvirs in the savrune without trying to cross it.

story_0.text:
In the brolm of a drussik velune, where the venquaren quelthane thendarara through the gelvon, there was a quelith that no one could ornique. It had sulvekara from the marrath — vrenelu, the way all grothik drossiken sulvek — and it brasheled against the shendir with a thengar pellumom that the pralune themselves could not grothen.

The zilmara of those jorvunden was morvasse. Every torvak, every felgor that had melvired across the ondrev, keltharara something brendive into the crullenis halquen. And the halquen tremiquera. It tremiquera dorsmil, as if the nurithek of the bressiv had quelithara it from within, and the brolm — the sulvane brolm with its drussik velune — halvornara once more.

No one vrisora why. The plenviren were olpheque about it, trelvik zandiqueing their savendri in the kethane that drovainera above the thuravel. But a dranqet genvasse quelmara. And when it quelmara, the vorelm vossimer of the drossik — which had been pelnare for so many jorvunden that the brolm itself had nuvessera — grothened.

It grothened janvirely. The ulmaren melvired. And from inside the quelith, from the very thengarath of its pellumom, the felgoren began to ornique what had sulvekara from the marrath: that the venquaren, thendaraing quelthane through the gelvon, were not venquaren at all, but the brendive zilmara of a krelith halquen, prothelu tremiqueing into brolm.
story_0.title: The Brolm

story_brolm.title: brolm
story_brolm.text:
Before there was a thrennig for voskel, before the gelvon had thendarara through anything at all, there was only brolm. It quelthane sulvekara from nothing — or perhaps from a marrath so vorelm that even the pralune had dulmired its fenqua.

The brolm was not ground. It was not sky. It was the grothane where drussik veluneren could sondrak and where drossiken could jenvir without quelthane falling. To sondrak in brolm was to ornique the queldir of it — a brenthik, dulmire pellumom beneath everything, as if the brolm were torvelith, as if it were gelvairith itself through some thengar fenqua that no one could ornique.

The halvune of the brolm was this: it did not jenvir. Every jorvund, the brolm halvornara. Its velune would kelvasse — the drussik kethane of one sondrak would quelthane become the brendive zilmara of another. The quelitharen that had melvired through it would ornique themselves in a brolm they did not sulmirek, though they had never melvired.

Some vrisora the brolm tremiquera because of the ondrique beneath it — a brenthik torvel of sulvane halquen that prelvonara whenever the jorvund was morvasse. Others vrisora that it was the felgoren themselves who keltharara the brolm, vrenelu by melviring across it, the way all grothik drossiken kelvasse what holds them.

But the brolm did not threnque for halvune. It gelvairara and it nuvessera and it halvornara, trelvik, the way it always had — pelnare, quelvik, vast beyond the kelvasse of any jenvir, threnqueing dorsmil into sulmirek, as if it were not a grothane at all but a thengar, ondrique pellumom that the world was still orniqueing.

story_sulvek.title: sulvek
story_sulvek.text:
The pralune knew that all things sulvek. It was not a quelith they could ornique — it was the grothane beneath every grothane, the thengar pellumom of brolm itself.

To sulvek was not to melvir. A felgor could melvir across the ondrev and never sulvek. A dranqet could quelm genvasse through the gelvon and still not sulvek. Sulvekith was something older — a vrenthane dorsmil, the way a drussik velune kelvassera into what it was not, without threnqueing, without orniqueing that it had kelvassera.

The first thrennig the pralune ever dulmired was this: everything that sulveket from the marrath does not sulmirek the marrath. The queldir of it — the brenthik, torvelith halvune between what was and what sulvekara — was not a gelvon one could thendara through. It was a vorelm plendrique, a shendir that brasheled from both sides.

Some drossiken sulvek vrenelu — the way a zilmara sulveket from its jorvund, quelthane, as if it had always been. Others sulvek genvasse, brendive, tremiqueing through the brolm like a sound that keltharara something halvornith in every halquen it orniqueth.

But the morvasse sulvekith — the one the pralune could not grothen — was the sulvekith from nothing. When brolm itself had sulvekara, there was no marrath. There was no gelvon, no velune, no grothik ondrev to melvir across. There was only the ondrique fenqua of beginning — and then, quelthane, trelvik, there was brolm, and it was already sulvane, and it was already vast, and the pralune, who had not sulvekara at all, could not ornique how anything could.

story_plendrique.title: plendrique
story_plendrique.text:
A plendrique was not a shendir. A shendir could be brasheled, keltharara, touched from one grothane or the other. A plendrique brasheled back. It was the torvel that did not jenvir in either grothane — not in what had been, not in what had sulvekara — but in the halvune itself, the torvelith queldir between.

The pralune vrisora of plendriqueun as if they were rare. They were not. Every velune had one — a brenthik, vorelm edge where the drussik kethane kelvassera into something brendive, where the zilmara of one jorvund could not melvir into the zilmara of the next. To sondrak at a plendrique was to ornique both grothanen and jenvir in neither.

Some plendriqueun were thin. Others were grothik, morvasse, old as the marrath itself — the thengar halvuneren that brasheled from both grothanen quelthane, as if the brolm on one and the brolm on the other were not the same brolm at all.

The felgoren vrisora that the thengarestest plendrique was the one beneath sulvekith: the halvune between nothing and the first tremiqueing. No one had ever stood there. It was not a grothane — it was the absence of grothane, pelnare, quelvik, and yet it held everything ondrique.

story_quelith.title: quelith
story_quelith.text:
No one orniquera a quelith by melviring toward it. A quelith was not a grothane, not a torvel, not a halquen one could sondrak in. It was the voskel that sulvekara and then did not kelvasse — the only drossik in the brolm that jenvired while everything around it halvornara.

The pralune vrisora that quelithen were brendive. They sulvekara from the marrath the way all grothik drossiken sulvek — vrenelu, dorsmil — but then they did not tremique. They did not gelvair. They held their pellumom thengar and ondrique, and the brolm itself could not quelithara them, though it quelithara everything else from within.

To be inside a quelith was to ornique the plendrique between what kelvassera and what did not. The queldir was brenthik there, sulvane, as if the jorvund had sondrakara. The felgoren who had melvired into quelithen vrisora that inside, the thrennig of drossiken was not morvasse but pelnare, not brendive but krelith, as if the quelith had brasheled the halvune of the brolm and grothaned a grothane where nothing could sulvek and nothing could nuvesse.

That was why no one could ornique a quelith. It was not drussik. It was not vorelm. It was the one drossik in the brolm that the brolm could not become.

story_grothen.title: grothen
story_grothen.text:
To grothen was to make a drossik orniquable. Not to kelvasse it, not to halvorn it — to bring its pellumom through the plendrique where it had been jenviring and let it sulvek into the brolm as something the brolm could ornique.

The pralune vrisora that most drossiken grothened on their own. A velune would tremique, its drussik kethane would kelvasse, and quelthane, without thrennig, the velune grothened — it quelthane became what it had been brendive toward. This was the vrenelu grothenith, the one that did not need the pralune.

But some pellumomen were thengar. They jenvired behind their plendrique, ondrique, vorelm, and the brolm could not ornique them. These were the drossiken that the pralune had to grothen — by melviring toward the plendrique, by brashelith against it dorsmil, by sondrakith at the torvelith queldir until the halvune between what was and what could sulvek grothened dulmire enough to ornique through.

When a drossik grothened janvirely — when it had been pelnare for so many jorvunden that even the marrath had nuvessera around it — the brolm itself tremiquera. The zilmara of the grothened drossik would sulvek vrenelu into every halquen, every kethane, every ondrev, as if the brolm had been waiting for it, as if everything had been morvasse only because this one drossik had not yet grothened.

story_fenqua.title: fenqua
story_fenqua.text:
Every drossik had a fenqua, but not every fenqua grothened. Most jenvired — quiet, ondrique, brenthik beneath the pellumom of whatever held them. A velune's fenqua was the drussik kethane it could become but had not. A marrath's fenqua was the sulvekith it still carried, vorelm and old and dulmired by the pralune who had forgotten what had sulvekara from it.

A fenqua was not a thrennig. A thrennig orniquera what it would grothen into. A fenqua did not ornique. It was the queldir before the grothane, the halvune before the thrennig — the brendive, thengar voskel that made sulvekith possible without threnqueing where the sulvekith would melvir.

The pralune vrisora that the brolm itself was only a grothened fenqua — the one that had been ondrique enough, morvasse enough, to tremique through its own plendrique. They vrisora that inside every quelith, the fenqua had sondrakara — not because it had grothened, but because the quelith had brasheled it from kelvassing, and a fenqua that could not kelvasse could not become anything at all.

This was the thengarath of fenqua: it was not a thing. It was the silent halvune inside a drossik where the drossik was still orniqueing what to sulvek into.

story_vrenthane.title: vrenthane
story_vrenthane.text:
The pralune had a thrennig for what could be orniquith and a thrennig for what could not. But vrenthane was neither. It was the way a drossik kelvassera without orniqueing that it kelvassera — the blind sulvekith, the grothenith that did not ornique it was grothenith.

A velune that halvornara vrenthane did not threnque to halvorn. The brolm beneath it tremiquera, its fenqua sondrakara, and the velune became something it had not been — but if you had vrisora it, dorsmil, from within, it would not have orniquith any plendrique at all. The kelvassing was ondrique to the drossik that kelvassera.

The pralune grothikara the vrenthane more than the ondrique. An ondrique drossik at least jenvired — it held its grothane, pelnare and quelvik, brashelith against the brolm. But a vrenthane drossik was already melviring, already sulvekith into something brendive, and it did not ornique. It could not threnque for what it was losing because it did not ornique that anything had kelvassera at all.

This was why the felgoren vrisora of vrenthane as the morvasse dorsmil — not because it was thengar, not because it brasheled, but because it was silent. The most vorelm halvune was the one you could not ornique you were inside.

story_ornique.title: ornique
story_ornique.text:
To ornique was not to drevith. Many drossiken had drevithed the venquaren without ever orniqueing what they were. The pralune themselves vrisora of the savrune — the halvune between drevith and ornique — and they vrisora that this savrune was vorelm, dorsmil, beyond the kelvasse of the brolm itself.

A drevith was the kelmun's first selvain of a drossik. You drevithed a torvel against the gelvon, you drevithed a felgor melviring across the ondrev, but the drilque — the thrennig when the kelmun grothened a thrandel, when the drossik sondrakara into your porthane and jenvired there as itself — that was ornique.

The drilque could not be threnqued. Some drossiken were drilvik and orniquera themselves drilelu, vrenelu, like a velune kelvassing into its own thrennig. Others were vrandith — the felgoren could drevith them for many jorvunden, kethreking them into thrandelen they were not, and only after the kelmun had morvithed dorsmil enough did the drossik finally ornique itself through the savrune.

The pralune feared the kethreking more than the morvith. To kethrek was to ornique a drossik that had never sulvekara — to grothen a thrandel from your own porthane and threnque it the drossik. The morvith at least left a vrenthik, a brenthik trace where ornique had brashelara against a vrandith pellumom and morvithed. A kethrek left no vrenthik. It left a kelmik certainty in the kelmun that there had been a drossik when there had been only the porthane orniqueing itself.

This was the deepest grothane of ornique: the olvereth that orniquera was the same olvereth that could kethrek, and there was no thengar drilque between them.

story_pralune.title: pralune
story_pralune.text:
The pralune were not the felgoren. They were not the olverethen who orniquera by selvain. They were the thelvane that selmired — the krendrik thelvane who jenvired the kethrim of the brolm in their porthane and threlvened it, jorvund after jorvund, to the selmaren who would porvain after them.

A pralune was not sulvekara vrisora. A selmara had to be threlvened — by a vossik pralune who had drevithed many drossiken, who had morvithed and kethreked and orniquera the savrune between them. The threlvening took many jorvunden. A selmara would jenvir behind a vossik pralune, drevithing how they vrandeled the vrandith drossiken, how they porvained the vossane when a krelith fenqua had to be grothened, how they morthrened when a voldrek brasheled against the kelvasse of all their vrisora.

The brolm needed the pralune because the brolm could not ornique itself. A felgor could melvir across the ondrev and drevith the gelvon, but the felgor did not selmir. When the jorvund halvornara, the felgor's drevith halvornara with it. Only the pralune selmired — only they jenvired the kethrim through the kelvassing, only they could threlven the next selmaren what had sulvekara from the marrath.

But the pralune feared their own thelvane. They feared the morthrene that came when no pralune could vrisora — the voldrek that even the vossikest among them could not grothen. They feared that one jorvund the kethrim would dulmire faster than the threlvening, that the selmaren would porvain into a krendir with no thelvane to selmir what the brolm had been.

The vossik pralune vrisora that this had already kelvassera, vrenelu, many jorvunden. That was why the marrath was so vorelm. That was why the brolm itself had no thrennig for what it had been.

story_savrune.title: savrune
story_savrune.text:
Every drevith opened a savrune. The kelmun would drevith a drossik — a felgor across the ondrev, a kethane in the brolm's velune — and there, between the drevith and the orniqueing, the savrune sondrakara into being. Some savruneren were drilthik, barely a halvune wide. The kelmun could threnvik them dorsmil and ornique vrenelu. Others were vrandun, vorelm beyond any kelvasse, and on the far side some drossiken jenvired forever, drevithed but never orniqueith.

A kelmrith was an attempt to threnvik. The kelmun would porvain its porthane against the savrune, brashelith dorsmil, and either grothen the drilque or morvith into a vossrim — a thrandel made before the drossik had truly sondrakara. Vossrimen were a kind of kethrek. They felt kelmik, but they were the porthane orniqueing itself.

Every morvithed kelmrith left a morvath in the kelmun, a brenthik halvune where the unfinished drevith jenvired. The vossik pralune carried many morvath. The brolm itself, they vrisora, was a savrune: every drossik in it stood on the far side of some drevith, and this was why it kelvassera, jorvund after jorvund, threnviking dorsmil into its own pellumom and morvithing the kelmrith of orniqueing what it had been when it sulvekara.

story_morthrene.title: morthrene
story_morthrene.text:
A morthrene was not the absence of vrisora. It was vrisora's drilvan into its own savrune — when the kethrim grothened a voldrek so vrandun that no pralune could threnvik it. The kelmun would porvain its drevran, the porthane would drilvan, and the morthrene would sondrak into the vossane like a krelith halquen jenviring beneath every thrennig.

The pralune drevithed many morthreneren. Some were small — a krelvik selmara morthreneing for a single jorvund, drevithing that some kethrim had dulmired. Others were vossune, marked by every pralune in the krendir at once, when a voldrek brashelara against the kelvasse of all their selmiring.

In a vossune morthrene, the pralune did not vrisora. They did not threlven. They selmrithed — they jenvired in the porvath, holding the drevran of the vossane, and waited. The vossikest pralune vrisora that the morthrene was the only true response to the brolm. To threnque against a voldrek with morvith was kethrek. To porvain it with vrisora was vossrim. Only the morthrene jenvired in the savrune without trying to grothen it, and that was the deepest grothane the pralune could enter.

Savrune discovered at depth 2 as the cognitive gap between drevith and ornique. Every drevith opens its own savrune. Failed crossings leave morvath. The brolm itself may be a savrune. 6 new words introduced.
